title: Handling Charged for Each Machine on a Renew Business Asset Buyback Collection
content:
The handling charged for each machine on a palletised collection is neither the programme's handling fee for a mailed-in device nor waived by the programme's waiver figure, and what it comes to is settled by the load alone: it follows the size of the load and whether the run finishes the batch. A full load is 20 machines. The machines already consented to on the agreement are the machines the shipment requests taken on it declare, less the machines the customer consents to hand over on this run, and never fewer than none.

1. Where the machines the customer consents to hand over are fewer than a full load and they leave machines of the agreement still to be consented to, the handling charged for each machine is the short load handling, being 3.50 USD.
2. Where the machines the customer consents to hand over are fewer than a full load and they finish the machines the agreement covers, the handling charged for each machine is the clearing load handling, being 2.40 USD.
3. Where the machines the customer consents to hand over are a full load or more, the handling charged for each machine is the standard handling, being 1.10 USD.

**Whether the run finishes the batch.** The machines already consented to on the agreement, taken together with the machines the customer consents to hand over on this run, are set against the machines the Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement covers. Where the two together come to fewer than the machines the agreement covers, machines are still to be consented to. Where they come to the machines the agreement covers or more, the run finishes them.

**Both sides of the full load.**

| Machines the customer consents to hand over | Machines of the agreement still to be consented to afterwards | Handling for each machine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 19 | yes | 3.50 USD |
| 19 | no | 2.40 USD |
| 20 | either way | 1.10 USD |
| 26 | either way | 1.10 USD |

A run of exactly 20 machines is a full load, so it is charged at 1.10 USD for each machine whether or not it finishes the batch; a run of 19 is fewer than a full load, and then it matters whether machines are left.

**Hypothetical illustration.** On an agreement covering 45 machines with 9 already consented to on earlier shipment requests, a run of 15 machines is fewer than a full load and brings the total consented to 24, leaving machines still to be consented to; the handling is 3.50 USD for each of the 15 machines, or 52.50 USD in all. A run of 36 on the same agreement is a full load or more, so the handling is 1.10 USD for each of the 36 machines, or 39.60 USD.
